md_name: Soil Metagenome and Environmental Context DAG
md_description: This workflow describes soil samples collected from multiple agricultural fields across locations and seasons, together with environmental descriptors measured at sampling. The soil is preprocessed, nucleic acids are extracted, and sequencing generates metagenomic reads. Downstream computation derives microbial community composition and diversity, which are integrated with soil pH, moisture, temperature, location, and time to study environmental drivers of microbial variation.

soil_sample.reasoning: This Entity node should describe the soil specimen itself: identity, provenance, collection context, and intrinsic sample attributes that are not measurements from later capture steps. I included sample identifiers and collection provenance because those belong to the root entity and are not repeated elsewhere. I also included fields needed to understand the specimen’s origin in an agricultural setting and the sample’s physical state at collection. I excluded soil pH, moisture, temperature, geographic location details as measured values, because those are owned by the downstream Capture/Signal nodes. I also excluded homogenization, extraction, sequencing, and any derived microbiome properties because those belong to downstream Process/Entity/Derivative nodes. No already_generated fields were provided, so there were no overlap constraints to apply.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the collected soil specimen; use a stable string such as "SS-001" or a site-lab accession code. Recorded once for the entity at sample creation and used to link all downstream processing, capture, and analysis records.

Date when the soil specimen was collected in the field, recorded at the time of sampling. Use ISO date format (YYYY-MM-DD); for example, 2026-05-14. Typical range spans the seasonal collection campaign.

Identifier for the agricultural field or sampling site where the soil specimen was obtained. Use a stable string code such as "FIELD_A03" or a site registry identifier. Recorded at collection and used to group samples by location.

Free-text or coded description of the collection location, such as farm name, field name, or broader geographic descriptor. Record at sampling time to preserve provenance of the specimen; may complement, but does not replace, precise coordinates stored elsewhere if present.
Season or campaign period associated with the collection event, used to track seasonal variation in soil specimens. Record at sampling time using one of the allowed categories.

Depth interval from which the soil specimen was collected, measured in centimeters at the field collection point. Report as a single depth or depth range, such as 0-10 cm, if the study standardizes sampling depth.

Descriptive soil class or texture of the collected specimen at the time of collection, if known from field notes or site classification. Record using a controlled term when possible, such as sandy loam, loam, clay loam, silt loam, clay, or other study-specific categories.

Mass of the collected soil specimen, measured in grams after field collection and before downstream homogenization or extraction. Typical values depend on the protocol and are often in the range of a few grams to hundreds of grams.

Method used to obtain the soil specimen in the field, recorded at sampling. Examples include core, auger, shovel, or hand-collected surface scrape; use the category that best matches the actual collection procedure.

Replicate index for the soil specimen within a site, depth, and time point, if multiple samples were collected under the same design. Use an integer starting at 1 to distinguish biological or field replicates.

Immediate preservation status of the soil specimen after collection and before downstream processing, indicating whether it was processed fresh, chilled, frozen, or otherwise stabilized. Record at collection or receipt to document handling of the entity itself.

soil_homogenization.reasoning: This Process node should describe how the soil sample was homogenized and aliquoted prior to extraction and measurement. I included operation parameters such as mixing conditions, aliquotting details, timing, and any QA/QC indicator because these are intrinsic to the process. I also included the responsible operator/instrument if applicable only insofar as they describe the operation. I excluded sample provenance fields because those belong to the upstream Entity node, and I excluded the homogenized material’s properties because those belong to the downstream Entity node. No already_generated fields were provided here, so there was no need to avoid named overlaps beyond the semantic separation required by the DAG.

md_schema.descr: Method used to mix and standardize the soil sample before downstream extraction or measurement. Record the actual procedure used in this workflow, such as manual mixing, mechanical shaking, bead-based mixing, or sieve-assisted homogenization.

Total time spent homogenizing the soil sample, measured in minutes from the start of mixing until the material was considered uniform and ready for aliquoting. Typical values are protocol-dependent and often range from a few minutes to tens of minutes.

Temperature of the soil material or work area during homogenization, measured in degrees Celsius at the time of processing when temperature is controlled or relevant to the protocol. Typical values are near ambient laboratory temperature unless chilled processing is used.

Number of aliquots produced from the homogenized soil sample for downstream extraction or measurement. Record as an integer count at the end of the homogenization step, before aliquots are distributed to later workflow nodes.

Mass of each aliquot generated from the homogenized soil, measured in grams after subdivision. If aliquots vary, record the nominal target mass used for the workflow, typically a fraction of the starting sample mass.

Name of the device or tool used to homogenize the soil sample, if instrumented equipment was used. Examples include a laboratory mixer, bead mill, or shaker model identifier, recorded for reproducibility of the process.

Quality indicator for the homogenized material immediately after processing, capturing whether the sample appeared uniform enough for extraction and measurement. Use a controlled categorical value based on the workflow's acceptance criteria.

homogenized_soil.reasoning: This Entity node should describe the homogenized soil as a processed intermediate material: what it is, how much of it exists, and its intrinsic post-homogenization state. I included fields that identify the aliquoted processed material and capture physical properties relevant to downstream extraction, such as material mass and uniformity. I excluded the mixing parameters themselves because those belong to the upstream homogenization Process node, and I excluded nucleic acid yield or sequencing suitability because those belong to downstream extraction and capture nodes. No already_generated fields were provided, so there were no duplication constraints beyond staying in the entity layer.

md_schema.descr: Identifier for the homogenized soil material after processing, used to distinguish this prepared entity from the original field-collected specimen. Use a stable string such as a lab accession suffix or aliquot label, for example "SS-001-H1".

Identifier of the original soil specimen from which this homogenized material was prepared. Use the upstream sample code such as "SS-001" to preserve provenance between the collected entity and the processed entity.

Total mass of the homogenized soil material available after mixing and aliquoting, measured in grams at the point the processed entity is created. Typical values depend on the protocol and starting sample size.

Index of the aliquot within the set generated from the homogenized soil, recorded as an integer at creation time. Use this to distinguish multiple processed portions derived from the same original sample.

Intrinsic assessment of how uniform the processed soil material is after homogenization, recorded as a property of the material itself rather than the procedure. Use a controlled categorical value reflecting whether the entity is suitable for downstream extraction and measurement.

Condition under which the homogenized soil entity is held before downstream extraction, such as refrigeration, freezing, or room-temperature short-term holding. Record the actual state of the processed material at the time it is handed off to the next workflow step.

Elapsed time that the homogenized soil has been held under its current storage condition before downstream processing, measured in hours from creation or receipt of the processed entity. Typical values range from minutes to days depending on workflow timing.

Type of subsample represented by this homogenized entity, if the workflow distinguishes among technical portions of the same soil material. Use a controlled label such as extraction_input, archive, or measurement_split as appropriate.

field_env_capture.reasoning: This Capture node should describe the field measurement session and instrument configuration used to record environmental context at sampling. I included the actively configured measurement channels and hardware/probe details, because capture nodes own how the measurements were obtained. I excluded the actual pH, moisture, temperature, location, and time values themselves because those belong on the downstream Signal node as raw environmental readings. I also excluded sample identity and soil provenance because those belong to the Entity node. No already_generated fields were provided, so there were no direct name conflicts to avoid.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the field environmental measurement session associated with a soil collection event. Use a stable string such as "ENV-2026-05-14-F01" to link the capture configuration to the raw environmental readings.

Time zone used to interpret the sampling timestamp recorded by the field instruments, specified at the capture session level. Use a standard zone label such as UTC, local site time, or an IANA time zone string if available.
Manufacturer of the field probe or instrument array used to measure environmental descriptors during soil sampling. Record the vendor name for the active capture hardware.
Model name or number of the field probe or instrument array used during environmental capture. Record the exact hardware model to support reproducibility of the measurement session.
Serial number of the field probe or instrument array used in the capture session. Record the manufacturer-assigned serial identifier as a string, for example "SN1234567".

Configured method or sensor mode used to measure soil pH during the field capture session. Examples include direct probe measurement or slurry-based field estimation, depending on the instrument setup.
Configured method or sensor mode used to measure soil moisture content during capture. Record the actual device mode used in the field, such as capacitance, gravimetric-support, or TDR-based sensing.
Type of sensor configured to record soil or near-sample temperature during the field capture session. Record the active sensor class or configuration used at measurement time.
How geographic location was captured during the field session, such as GPS, GNSS, or manually entered site coordinates. This describes the capture configuration, not the location value itself.
Resolution of the recorded sampling time in the capture session, such as seconds or minutes. Record the precision supported by the instrument or workflow used to timestamp the field measurements.

Operator- or instrument-assigned quality indicator for the field environmental capture session, reflecting whether the readings were complete and technically acceptable before being written as raw signal. Use the workflow's control categories.

env_signal.reasoning: This Signal node should describe the raw environmental data artifact produced by the field capture session: file/record format, dimensions, location in storage, and technical quality of the raw readings. I included raw data structure fields and technical file attributes because those belong to the signal layer. I excluded the measured environmental values themselves because those are scientific content derived from the capture and are better represented as the raw signal payload rather than as capture settings; however, I avoided repeating the exact measurement variables as separate schema fields because the capture node already owns the configured channels and the downstream user mainly needs to know how the raw artifact is stored and organized. I excluded sample provenance and instrument configuration because those belong to the Entity and Capture nodes respectively. No already_generated fields were provided, so there were no duplicate-field constraints beyond maintaining the signal-only scope.

md_schema.descr: Name of the raw environmental data file or record bundle generated by the field capture session. Use the exact filename or record label as stored, for example "env_readings_2026-05-14.csv".
File format of the raw environmental measurements artifact written by the capture system. Record the actual technical format used for storage or interchange, such as CSV, TSV, JSON, or XML.
Size of the raw environmental data file, measured in bytes at the time of storage or export. Record the technical artifact size for downstream data management and transfer planning.
Number of raw environmental records or rows contained in the signal artifact, counted after the field capture session completes. Use this to describe the dimensionality of the raw data bundle.

Number of data columns or fields present in the raw environmental signal artifact, counted in the stored file or table. This describes the structure of the raw measurement record without interpreting the values.

Storage location of the raw environmental data artifact, such as a file path, object-store URI, or database pointer. Use the exact accessible location string, for example "s3://bucket/path/env_readings.csv" or "/data/run1/env.csv".
Integrity checksum for the raw environmental data artifact, recorded after file creation or transfer. Use a string hash such as MD5 or SHA-256 to verify the exact raw signal content.

Technical quality indicator for the raw environmental signal artifact, reflecting completeness, corruption, or readability of the stored data. Use a controlled category assigned after capture and file validation.

Start time covered by the raw environmental measurements in the stored artifact, recorded as the earliest timestamp present in the signal. Use ISO 8601 datetime if available, or a date-time string consistent with the workflow.

End time covered by the raw environmental measurements in the stored artifact, recorded as the latest timestamp present in the signal. Use ISO 8601 datetime if available, or a date-time string consistent with the workflow.

nucleic_acid_extraction.reasoning: This Process node should describe how nucleic acids were extracted from the homogenized soil: the protocol, reagents/kit, key parameters, operator/software agent if relevant, and an output quality indicator. I included extraction chemistry and handling parameters because those are the process territory. I excluded the extracted DNA/RNA material’s identity, yield-as-an-entity properties, and downstream sequencing details because those belong to the output Entity node or later Capture node. No already_generated fields were provided, so there were no name conflicts to avoid.

md_schema.descr: Name of the nucleic acid extraction protocol used on the homogenized soil. Record the actual workflow or kit protocol, for example a soil DNA extraction method name or validated laboratory SOP identifier.
Manufacturer or vendor of the extraction kit or consumables used in this process, if applicable. Record the supplier name at the time of extraction to support reproducibility.
Commercial name or model of the nucleic acid extraction kit used for the soil extraction process. Record the exact kit name when a kit-based workflow is used.

Mass of homogenized soil used as input to the extraction process, measured in grams at the start of extraction. Typical values are protocol dependent and often fall in the range of fractions of a gram to several grams.
Method used to break open cells and release nucleic acids during extraction. Record the actual lysis strategy applied in the process, such as chemical, mechanical, enzymatic, or combined lysis.

Temperature used during any extraction incubation step, measured in degrees Celsius while the sample is being processed. Typical values depend on the protocol and may include room temperature or heated incubation conditions.
Duration of the extraction incubation or lysis period, measured in minutes from the start to the end of the timed step. Typical values range from minutes to hours depending on the protocol.

Final elution volume used to recover nucleic acids from the extraction, measured in microliters at the end of the process. Record the actual volume used to resuspend or collect the extracted material.
Person or automated system responsible for carrying out the nucleic acid extraction process. Record a name, initials, or system identifier as used in the laboratory workflow.

Process-level quality indicator summarizing whether the extraction produced analyzable nucleic acid material suitable for downstream sequencing. Use the workflow acceptance categories assigned after extraction completion.

soil_nucleic_acids.reasoning: This Entity node should describe the extracted nucleic-acid material itself: what it is, how much material exists, what fraction is DNA versus RNA if known, and its intrinsic quality/state after extraction. I included yield, concentration, purity, and storage attributes because they are properties of the extracted material entity. I excluded the extraction protocol, reagents, and incubation settings because those belong to the upstream extraction Process node, and I excluded sequencing instrument settings because those belong to the downstream sequencing Capture node. No already_generated fields were provided, so there were no overlap constraints to resolve.

md_schema.descr: Identifier for the extracted nucleic-acid material prepared from a soil sample. Use a stable string such as "NA-SS-001-01" or the laboratory accession assigned to the extract.
Identifier of the homogenized soil material from which the nucleic acids were extracted. Use the upstream processed sample code to preserve provenance between the soil entity and the extract entity.

Type of nucleic-acid material represented by this entity, indicating whether the extract contains DNA, RNA, or a mixed nucleic-acid preparation. Record the actual material class produced by the workflow.

Total nucleic-acid yield obtained from the soil extraction, measured in nanograms at the point the extract entity is created or quantified. Typical values depend on soil biomass and protocol efficiency and may range from very low to high recoveries.

Concentration of the extracted nucleic-acid material, measured in nanograms per microliter after extraction and any resuspension step. Record the quantified concentration used to prepare downstream sequencing input.

Spectrophotometric purity ratio A260/A280 for the extracted nucleic acids, measured after extraction and before sequencing preparation. Typical values near 1.8 are often expected for DNA-rich extracts, but acceptable ranges depend on the workflow.

Spectrophotometric purity ratio A260/A230 for the extracted nucleic acids, measured after extraction and before sequencing preparation. This ratio helps assess contamination by salts, organics, or other carryover from soil extraction.

Storage condition of the nucleic-acid extract after preparation and before sequencing, such as refrigerated or frozen. Record the condition of the material entity at the handoff to downstream processing.

Volume of the recovered nucleic-acid extract, measured in microliters at the point the entity is characterized or passed to the next step. This is the total liquid volume containing the extracted material.

Intrinsic integrity assessment of the extracted nucleic-acid material, reflecting whether the extract appears intact and suitable for sequencing or other downstream use. Use a controlled categorical assessment assigned after extraction QC.

sequencing_capture.reasoning: This Capture node should describe the sequencing session and instrument configuration used to read the extracted soil nucleic acids. I included sequencer hardware identifiers, run configuration, chemistry, read settings, lane/cell usage, and operator-controlled settings because those define the capture environment. I excluded the raw read file properties and technical file metrics because those belong to the downstream Signal node. I also excluded the nucleic-acid sample properties and extraction quality because those belong to the upstream Entity node. No already_generated fields were provided, so there were no duplicate-field constraints to apply.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the sequencing capture session or run associated with this soil nucleic-acid sample. Use a stable string such as "RUN_2026_05_14_A" to link instrument settings to the generated raw reads.
Manufacturer of the sequencing instrument used for the capture session. Record the vendor name of the active sequencer hardware.
Model name or number of the sequencing instrument used in this run. Record the exact sequencer model for reproducibility of the capture session.
Serial number of the sequencing instrument used in the capture session. Record the manufacturer-assigned serial identifier as a string, for example "SN123456".
Sequencing chemistry or library readout chemistry configured for the capture session. Record the actual chemistry used, such as short-read paired-end chemistry or another run-specific configuration.

Configured read length in base pairs for each sequencing read produced by the instrument during the capture session. Typical values depend on the platform and assay and should reflect the setting used for this run.
Whether the sequencing run was configured to produce paired-end reads. Record true if the instrument collected reads from both ends of each fragment, otherwise false.
Identifier for the flow cell, lane, or equivalent consumable used in the sequencing capture session. Record the exact device partition or run unit used to generate the raw metagenomic data.
Library concentration loaded onto the sequencer for this capture session, measured in pM at run setup. Typical values are platform-dependent and affect cluster or molecule loading efficiency.
Named settings profile or preset applied to the sequencing instrument during the run, if such a profile was used. Record the active configuration that governed run behavior, not the output data.

Run-level quality indicator assigned immediately after the sequencing capture session, reflecting whether the instrument run completed successfully and was suitable for downstream raw read generation. Use the workflow's control categories.

raw_reads.reasoning: I removed the colliding field read_length_bp because it had already been generated earlier in the DAG. The remaining fields stay within the raw signal territory: file identity, format, size, counts, storage, checksum, technical quality, and linkage back to the run. I kept the description of read size/counts and omitted any capture-level chemistry or downstream interpretation, preserving the signal-only scope.

md_schema.descr: Name of the raw metagenomic sequencing reads file as stored by the workflow. Use the exact filename or primary archive label, for example "sample01_R1.fastq.gz" or a run-specific bundle name.
File format of the raw read artifact generated by sequencing. Record the exact technical format used for storage or interchange, such as FASTQ, BAM, or CRAM.
Size of the raw sequencing read file, measured in bytes after generation or transfer. Record the technical artifact size for downstream data management and storage planning.
Total number of raw sequencing reads contained in the artifact, counted at the point the raw data file is finalized. Use this as a structural measure of the signal output.

Number of read pairs present when the raw sequencing data were generated as paired-end reads. Record zero or omit conceptually if the run was single-end, but store the actual count when paired-end is used.

Storage location of the raw sequencing reads artifact, such as a file path, object-store URI, or database pointer. Use the exact accessible location string, for example "s3://bucket/path/sample01.fastq.gz" or "/data/run1/sample01.fastq.gz".
Integrity checksum for the raw sequencing read artifact, recorded after file creation or transfer. Use a string hash such as MD5 or SHA-256 to verify that the stored file has not been altered.

Technical quality indicator for the raw reads file, reflecting whether the sequence data are complete and readable at the signal stage. Use a controlled category assigned after file validation and basic run checks.

Identifier of the sequencing run that produced this raw read artifact, used to connect the signal back to the capture session. Use the run ID assigned by the instrument or LIMS, such as "RUN_2026_05_14_A".

read_processing.reasoning: This Process node should describe how raw sequencing reads were filtered and prepared for downstream analysis: trimming/filtering method, software/pipeline agent, key thresholds, and process-level output quality. I excluded raw read file properties because those belong to the upstream Signal node, and I excluded community profiles or diversity outcomes because those belong to downstream nodes. I also avoided the previously generated field name read_length_bp by using process-specific trimming length fields instead of repeating the raw read measurement.

md_schema.descr: Name of the read-processing pipeline or workflow used to filter and prepare sequencing reads. Record the actual pipeline name used in this step, such as a laboratory SOP name or a bioinformatics workflow label.
Software name used to execute the read-processing step. This belongs on the Process node because it describes the computational agent carrying out the filtering and trimming operation.
Version of the software or pipeline used for read processing, recorded at the time the process was run. Include the exact version string to support reproducibility.
Repository, package source, or code location for the read-processing workflow, if applicable. Record the source used to obtain the processing software or pipeline implementation.

Configured quality threshold used to remove low-quality reads or bases during processing, recorded at the point of filtering. Typical values may be Phred score cutoffs or similar platform-specific thresholds.
Whether adapter trimming was enabled during read processing. Record true if adapters were removed as part of the workflow, otherwise false.

Minimum read length in base pairs required after trimming for a read to be retained in the processed set. Record the process parameter used to filter reads after preprocessing, not the length of the raw input reads.
Whether reads matching host or non-target sequences were removed during processing. Record true if filtering against a host or contaminant database was performed, otherwise false.
Whether duplicate reads were collapsed or dereplicated during preprocessing. Record true if identical reads were removed or merged as part of the workflow, otherwise false.

Process-level quality indicator summarizing whether the read-processing step produced an adequate set of cleaned reads for downstream community analysis. Use the workflow's acceptance categories after processing completes.

processed_reads.reasoning: This Signal node should describe the cleaned/trimmed read artifact itself: its file identity, format, size, structure, storage, and technical quality after processing. I included fields that capture the processed data object and its integrity. I excluded upstream processing parameters because those belong on the read_processing Process node, and I excluded downstream feature or community interpretation because those belong on derivative nodes. I also avoided repeating the previously generated read_length_bp field by using processed-read-specific length fields instead.

md_schema.descr: Name of the cleaned and trimmed read file as stored by the workflow. Use the exact filename or archive label, for example "sample01_trimmed.fastq.gz".
File format of the processed read artifact after filtering and trimming. Record the exact technical format used for storage or interchange, such as FASTQ, BAM, CRAM, or similar.
Size of the processed read file, measured in bytes after cleaning and trimming. Record the technical artifact size for downstream storage and transfer planning.
Total number of cleaned sequencing reads contained in the processed artifact, counted after trimming and filtering are complete. Use this as a structural measure of the signal output.
Number of read pairs present in the processed artifact when the data were generated as paired-end reads. Record the actual count after filtering and trimming.

Observed or reported length of reads in the processed artifact, measured in base pairs after trimming and cleaning. This field describes the technical output length of the processed reads, not the original raw input length.

Storage location of the processed read artifact, such as a file path, object-store URI, or database pointer. Use the exact accessible location string, for example "s3://bucket/path/sample01_trimmed.fastq.gz" or "/data/run1/sample01_trimmed.fastq.gz".
Integrity checksum for the processed read artifact, recorded after file creation or transfer. Use a string hash such as MD5 or SHA-256 to verify that the stored file has not been altered.

Technical quality indicator for the processed read file, reflecting whether the cleaned data are complete, readable, and suitable for downstream feature derivation. Use a controlled category assigned after post-processing validation.

Identifier of the upstream processing run that produced this cleaned read artifact, used to link the signal back to the read-processing process. Use the pipeline or run identifier assigned by the workflow system.

community_profiling.reasoning: This Process node should describe how processed reads were converted into microbial abundance and taxonomic profiles: the profiling algorithm/workflow, software agent, reference database, key thresholds, and process-level output quality. I excluded the input read file properties because those belong to the upstream Signal node, and I excluded the resulting abundance table or taxonomy profile as an output object because those belong to the downstream Derivative node. I also avoided any field names already generated for prior steps, including read_length_bp and related read artifact fields, by focusing only on profiling-specific computation parameters.

md_schema.descr: Name of the community profiling workflow used to convert processed reads into microbial abundance and taxonomic outputs. Record the actual pipeline or analysis label used in this step.
Software name used to perform the community profiling process. This belongs on the Process node because it identifies the computational agent that generated taxonomic or abundance estimates.
Version of the profiling software or pipeline used at the time the process was run. Record the exact version string to support reproducibility.
Repository, package source, or implementation location for the profiling workflow, if applicable. Record where the profiling code or package was obtained.
Reference database used to assign taxonomy or quantify microbial features during profiling. Record the database name used by the workflow, such as a curated taxonomic reference or marker database.
Version or release date of the reference database used in community profiling. Record the exact database version to support reproducibility of the derived taxonomy and abundance assignments.

Similarity or identity threshold used for assigning reads to taxa or feature groups during profiling, recorded as a percentage. Typical values depend on the method and database, and this threshold should reflect the parameter used in the analysis.

Minimum alignment or query coverage required for assigning a read to a taxon or feature during profiling, recorded as a percentage. This parameter governs how strict the mapping step is in the process.

Method used to normalize read counts or feature abundances during the profiling step. Record the actual normalization strategy applied, such as raw counts, relative abundance, compositional scaling, or other workflow-specific methods.

Process-level quality indicator summarizing whether the community profiling step produced interpretable abundance and taxonomic outputs suitable for downstream derivative analyses. Use the workflow's acceptance categories after profiling completes.

microbial_profile.reasoning: This Derivative node should describe the computed microbial community profile itself: what algorithm produced it, the output table structure, taxonomic resolution, and derived summary quality indicators. I included fields that characterize the derived abundance/profile artifact and its interpretability. I excluded the raw processed reads and profiling parameters because those belong to the upstream Process and Signal nodes. I also avoided repeating any previously generated read artifact fields, including read_length_bp, by staying in the derivative territory and using profile-specific dimensions instead.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the derived microbial community profile. Use a stable string such as "MP-SS-001" or an analysis accession that ties the profile to the sample and profiling run.
Identifier of the processed read artifact used to compute this microbial profile. Use the upstream processed-read accession to preserve provenance from signal to derivative.

Name of the algorithm or method used to derive the microbial community profile from processed reads. Record the actual method label used in the analysis, such as a taxonomic assignment or abundance-estimation approach.

Lowest or primary taxonomic rank represented in the derived profile, recorded as the resolution used for abundance summarization. Use a controlled value that matches the granularity of the output table.
Number of microbial features represented in the derived profile, counted as rows, taxa, or equivalent units in the output table. This is a structural property of the computed derivative.
Number of samples represented in the derived profile matrix or table, counted as columns or sample entries after computation. Record the output matrix size at the derivative stage.
Units used to express microbial feature abundances in the derived profile. Record the actual output scale used by the analysis, such as counts, proportions, or percentages.
Proportion of zero-valued entries in the derived abundance table, measured as a percentage of all feature-by-sample cells. This is a derived data-quality indicator for profile interpretability.

Shannon diversity value calculated from the derived microbial profile for the focal sample or summarized profile, measured as a dimensionless index. Record the computed value if the profile node stores sample-level diversity summaries alongside abundance information.

Derived quality indicator for whether the microbial profile is sufficiently complete and interpretable for downstream ecological analysis. Use a controlled category assigned after profile generation and validation.

diversity_analysis.reasoning: This Process node should describe how microbial profiles were analyzed to compute alpha/beta diversity and compare communities across samples. I included the analysis method, software agent, diversity metrics calculated, distance/dissimilarity choices, and process-level output quality because those are the process territory. I excluded the actual diversity values and comparison results because those belong to the downstream Derivative node. I also excluded upstream profile properties because those belong to the microbial_profile derivative. No already_generated fields were provided for this step, so there were no direct name conflicts to avoid.

md_schema.descr: Name of the diversity-analysis workflow used to compute alpha and beta diversity from microbial profiles. Record the actual pipeline or analysis label used in this step.

Software name used to perform the diversity analysis process. This belongs on the Process node because it identifies the computational agent that calculated diversity metrics and community comparisons.
Version of the diversity-analysis software or pipeline used at the time the process was run. Record the exact version string to support reproducibility.
Repository, package source, or implementation location for the diversity-analysis workflow, if applicable. Record where the analysis code or package was obtained.
Name of the alpha diversity metric computed during this analysis step. Record the metric actually used, such as observed features, Shannon, Simpson, or another workflow-specific measure.
Name of the beta diversity or distance metric used to compare samples in this analysis step. Record the actual dissimilarity measure applied, such as Bray-Curtis, Jaccard, or UniFrac.

Sequencing or profile depth used for rarefaction before computing diversity metrics, measured as the number of reads or features retained per sample. Typical values depend on the dataset and analysis design.
Number of permutations used in any significance testing or community comparison performed during the diversity analysis. Record the actual count used by the statistical procedure.

Covariates included in the diversity analysis design matrix or comparison model, such as field, season, or sample group. Record the set of contextual variables used to stratify or adjust the community comparison.

Process-level quality indicator summarizing whether the diversity analysis completed successfully and produced statistically interpretable results. Use the workflow's acceptance categories after analysis completes.

diversity_results.reasoning: This Derivative node should describe the computed diversity and composition results themselves: the diversity values, ordination/comparison outputs, dimensions, and derived quality indicators. I included output-specific summary statistics and matrix/plot dimensions because those are properties of the computed result artifact. I excluded analysis settings, software, and permutation parameters because those belong to the upstream diversity_analysis Process node. I also excluded raw profile properties because those belong to the microbial_profile derivative. No already_generated fields were provided, so there were no direct collisions to avoid.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the derived diversity-results object. Use a stable string such as "DIV-SS-001" or an analysis accession that ties the results to the source microbial profile and analysis run.
Identifier of the microbial community profile used to compute these diversity results. Use the upstream profile accession to preserve provenance from profile to derivative.
Computed alpha diversity value for the sample or profile, measured as a dimensionless index produced by the diversity analysis. Typical values depend on the chosen metric, such as Shannon or Simpson.

Summary of beta diversity or between-sample dissimilarity associated with this result object, reported as a derived numeric value or compact summary of pairwise distances. Use the value produced by the analysis for the focal sample or result set.

Derived summary of microbial community composition across fields or seasons, such as dominant taxa, group-level abundance patterns, or compositional shifts. Store a concise textual or coded summary of the computed result.
Number of ordination axes retained in the diversity result output, counted at the point the derivative object is created. This describes the dimensionality of the computed comparison result.
Number of samples represented in the diversity-results object, counted from the computed comparison set. Record the size of the result set rather than the upstream profile matrix.
Number of microbial features or taxa summarized in the diversity-results object, counted at output generation. This field reflects the scope of the derived result artifact.
Number of comparison groups included in the diversity result, such as fields, seasons, or site classes. Record the group count used in the derived output.

Derived quality indicator for whether the diversity-results object is complete, interpretable, and suitable for downstream association analyses. Use the workflow's acceptance categories assigned after result generation.

joint_association_model.reasoning: This is the joint statistical/modeling Process node. I retained only fields that describe the model setup, inputs, software, and fit status, while removing the colliding permutation_count field and any derivative-level outputs. I also kept predictor/response specification and covariate adjustment because these define the process itself. No already_generated list was provided in this turn, but I honored the reported DAG-wide collision by renaming the resampling field to a model-specific bootstrap/resample counter rather than reusing permutation_count.

md_schema.descr: Name of the joint association model or statistical workflow used to combine environmental readings with microbial results. Record the actual model label or analysis name used in this step.
Software name used to run the environmental association modeling process. This belongs on the Process node because it identifies the computational agent that fit the model.
Version of the modeling software or pipeline used at the time the process was run. Record the exact version string to support reproducibility.
Repository, package source, or implementation location for the association-model workflow, if applicable. Record where the modeling code or package was obtained.

Name of the microbial response variable used in the association model, such as community composition, diversity index, or a specific abundance summary. Record the modeled microbial outcome as defined in the analysis.

Set of environmental predictor variables included in the association model, such as pH, moisture, temperature, location, and sampling time/season. Record the variables actually used in the fitted model.
Statistical model class used to combine environmental and microbial data. Record the actual model family or framework applied in this process step.
Whether the association model included adjustment for additional covariates or blocking factors, such as field identity, season, or batch. Record true if such adjustment was applied, otherwise false.

Number of bootstrap or resampling iterations used in model validation or internal stability checks for the association analysis, if applicable. Record the actual count used by the procedure when resampling is performed.

Process-level quality indicator summarizing whether the joint association model converged and produced interpretable results suitable for downstream derivative reporting. Use the workflow's acceptance categories after model fitting completes.

association_results.reasoning: This Derivative node should describe the computed statistical association results themselves: effect estimates, significance, model fit summaries, and the set of environmental drivers tested. I included output-level result fields because those belong to the derivative artifact. I excluded modeling choices, software, and resampling settings because those belong to the upstream joint_association_model Process node, and I excluded raw environmental and microbial source properties because they belong to env_signal and diversity_results. I also avoided the previously generated field permutation_count by using result-oriented summary fields rather than repeating process parameters.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the derived environmental association results object. Use a stable string such as "ASSOC-SS-001" or an analysis accession that links the results to the source model run.
Identifier of the environmental signal artifact used in the association analysis. Use the upstream raw environmental data accession to preserve provenance from field capture to derivative.

Identifier of the diversity-results object used as the microbial input to the association analysis. Use the upstream diversity result accession to preserve provenance from microbial summary to derivative.

Set of environmental variables evaluated in the association results, such as pH, moisture, temperature, location, and sampling time or season. Record the actual variables included in the final interpreted output.
Number of environmental variables found to be statistically significant in the association results, counted after model fitting and correction steps. Use this as a summary of the derivative output.

Summary of association effect sizes between environmental variables and microbial response, expressed in the units or standardized scale produced by the analysis. Store a concise numeric summary or compact text representation of the derived effects.

Smallest p-value reported among the environmental associations in the derivative results, recorded after statistical testing and any correction steps. Use this as a summary indicator of the strongest association signal.

Multiple-testing correction method applied to the association results, if used, recorded as a categorical description of the adjustment procedure. This is a property of the derived result interpretation rather than the fitting process.
Proportion or percentage of microbial variation explained by the environmental association model, measured at the result stage. Record the derived fit summary produced by the completed analysis.

Derived quality indicator summarizing whether the association results are complete, statistically interpretable, and suitable for reporting. Use the workflow's acceptance categories assigned after result generation.
